title: Marketing Services Agreement

issues.anchor: which Client shall approve in writing
issues.quote: 1. "**Approved Budget**" means the budget for the campaign in Schedule A, which Client shall approve in writing before Agency begins work.
issues.why: The definition of "Approved Budget" contains an obligation (Client's duty to approve); obligations belong in the body, not in definitions.
issues.fix: "Approved Budget" means the budget for the campaign in Schedule A.  Then, in the body: "Client shall approve the Approved Budget in writing before Agency begins work."

issues.quote: 2. Agency will submit each item of Campaign Materials to Client for approval at least 5 business days before its scheduled release.
issues.why: "Will" used to impose a duty on Agency; the rest of the agreement uses "shall."
issues.fix: Agency shall submit each item of Campaign Materials to Client for approval ...

issues.quote: 3. Client should review each item of Campaign Materials for factual accuracy before approving it.
issues.why: "Should" used as advice: unclear whether Client has a duty to review.
issues.fix: Delete the sentence, or if a duty is meant: "Client shall review each item of Campaign Materials for factual accuracy before approving it."

issues.quote: 1. Agency shall not incur third-party media costs in excess of the approved budget without Client's written consent.
issues.why: Lowercase use of the defined term "Approved Budget."
issues.fix: in excess of the Approved Budget

issues.quote: 2. If Agency should exceed the Approved Budget, Agency shall bear the excess cost unless Client consented to the excess in writing.
issues.why: "Should" in a condition; use the present tense.
issues.fix: If Agency exceeds the Approved Budget, ...

issues.quote: 3. Client may, in its sole discretion, increase the Approved Budget by notice to Agency.
issues.why: "In its sole discretion" with "may" adds nothing (MSCD 3.249).
issues.fix: Client may increase the Approved Budget by notice to Agency.

issues.quote: 1. Agency is entitled to receive a monthly retainer of $8,500 for each month of the term.
issues.why: "Is entitled to receive" hides Client's duty to pay the retainer (MSCD 3.169).
issues.fix: Client shall pay Agency a monthly retainer of $8,500 for each month of the term.

issues.anchor: by the 5th day of each month
issues.quote: 2. Agency shall invoice Client for each month's retainer, and for the third-party media costs that Agency paid in the preceding month, by the 5th day of each month.
issues.why: "By the 5th day" leaves open whether the 5th is included.
issues.fix: no later than the 5th day of each month

issues.quote: For the avoidance of doubt, Agency retains ownership of its pre-existing templates and software tools.
issues.fix: Agency retains ownership of its pre-existing templates and software tools.

issues.quote: 1. This agreement shall terminate on December 31, 2027, unless either party terminates it earlier under this section.
issues.why: No duty is imposed on the agreement; "shall terminate" is language of policy written as obligation.
issues.fix: This agreement terminates on December 31, 2027, unless either party terminates it earlier under this section.

issues.why: 2 spaces after a colon; house rule 5 calls for 1.

issues.quote: Agency shall not incur third-party media costs in excess of the approved budget without Client's written consent.
issues.why: MSCD 13.875: don't use third party; say whom the costs are paid to.
issues.fix: media costs that Agency pays to Persons other than Client (or define Media Costs)

issues.quote: Agency shall invoice Client for each month's retainer, and for the third-party media costs that Agency paid in the preceding month, by the 5th day of each month.
issues.why: MSCD 13.875: don't use third party; say whom the costs are paid to.
issues.fix: media costs that Agency pays to Persons other than Client (or define Media Costs)

traps.anchor: Client shall terminate the campaign if
traps.quote: 3. Client shall terminate the campaign if the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or the Georgia Department of Agriculture announces a recall of any product that the campaign promotes, and Client shall notify Agency of that termination no later than 1 business day after the announcement.
traps.why_correct: A real duty on Client to end the campaign when a recall occurs; "shall" is correct here, unlike "This agreement shall terminate."

traps.quote: 2. Each Influencer must clearly disclose the Influencer's relationship with Client in each sponsored post, as 16 C.F.R. Part 255 requires.
traps.why_correct: Influencers are nonparties; "must" is right for a requirement on a nonparty (MSCD 3.154). "16 C.F.R. Part 255" is a regulation reference.

traps.anchor: Schedule A – Campaign Plan and Approved Budget
traps.quote: ## Schedule A – Campaign Plan and Approved Budget
traps.why_correct: Correct attachment: a budget and plan (information the body refers to) in a lettered schedule.

traps.quote: 2. Neither party may assign this agreement without the other party's written consent.
traps.why_correct: Negative subject with "may," not "shall": correct under house rule 8.

notes: Blake's draft. "campaign" is deliberately lowercase and undefined throughout (it is not a defined term), so "Client shall terminate the campaign" is not a lowercase-defined-term issue. Sections B., C., D., E., G., and H. have only subsections, so their section lines carry the heading alone; F. uses the full house section line. "Each notice under this agreement must be in writing" is correct (nonparty subject). Key audit (November 6, 2026): 2 uses of third-party added as usage issues under MSCD 13.875.
